Philosophy Quotes About Peace

Peace names both a political condition and a settled mind. Epicurean ataraxia, Stoic equanimity, and East Asian calm each propose different disciplines for reducing unnecessary disturbance.

Quotes / About / Peace

16 quotations on peace

  1. Death is nothing to us: for what has been dissolved has no sensation, and what has no sensation is nothing to us.
    Epicurus
    Death
  2. Pleasure is the beginning and end of the happy life — not the pleasures of profligates, but freedom from pain in the body and from disturbance in the soul.
    Epicurus
    Life
  3. With whatever delights you, remind yourself of its nature — then if it is lost, you will not be disturbed.
    Epictetus
    Philosophy
  4. Therefore death is nothing to us, and does not concern us at all.
    Lucretius
    Death
  5. Do not seek for things to happen as you wish, but wish for things to happen as they do, and you will flow well.
    Epictetus
    Philosophy
  6. Depart then in peace; the one who releases you is also at peace.
    Marcus Aurelius
    Death
  7. To establish the mind for Heaven and Earth; to secure the destiny of the people; to continue the interrupted learning of the past sages; to open peace for all ages.
    Zhang Zai
    Philosophy
  8. Pleasant it is, when winds trouble the great sea, to gaze from shore upon another's great tribulation.
    Lucretius
    Philosophy
  9. The quest for certainty…has always been a quest for a peace that is assured.
    John Dewey
    Certainty
  10. I shall endeavor not to laugh at human actions, nor to weep over them, nor to hate them, but to understand them.
    Baruch Spinoza
    Understanding
  11. The quest for certainty…is a quest for a peace which is assured.
    John Dewey
    Certainty
  12. Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same…
    Bhagavad Gita
    Equanimity
  13. This mind is luminous—what more is there to say?
    Wang Yangming
    Self
  14. Hatreds never cease through hatred in this world.
    Dhammapada
    Philosophy
  15. Contacts with the senses, O son of Kunti, give cold and heat, pleasure and pain; they come and go — endure them.
    Bhagavad Gita
    Endurance
  16. Do not be troubled about whether the rest of life will be long or short, as if that mattered much.
    Marcus Aurelius
    Time
